title: Command palette
description: Cmd+K command palette. Signs commands into `@wordpress/commands`; derives palette entries from `config.commands[]` + `config.screens[]`.

documentation.purpose: Cmd+K command palette contributor. The palette UI itself is owned by `@wordpress/commands` — this app contributes a command set and renders nothing. Two v3 sources feed the palette: (1) `config.commands[]` — labelled first-class commands (v3 replacement for v2's `bindings` array); entries with a `label` become palette entries, callback fires `invoke` then `navigate` matching `BindingsConsumer`'s keystroke-handler order. (2) `config.screens[]` — every non-hidden screen with a `path` + `label` becomes a `Go to <label>` entry; hidden / parameterized / wildcarded paths skipped. Two dedup layers stack: dedup-by-path (a command's `navigate` suppresses a screen entry on the same path) + dedup-by-name (the unified `core/admin-shell/palette-<id>` prefix catches id collisions across sources, first-write wins). The branching is unit-testable on a bare Node runtime via the pure-ESM compiler at `compileCommands.mjs`.

reads.purpose: First-class commands (id + label + optional shortcut + invoke|navigate). Labelled entries surface in the palette; keyboard-only entries (no label) are handled by `BindingsConsumer` and never appear here.
Workspace screen map. Each entry with a `path` + `label` (and not `hidden: true`, not parameterized) becomes a synthesized `Go to <label>` palette entry.

writes.purpose: Register the derived command set via `useCommandLoader({ name: 'core/admin-shell/apps', hook })`.

states.renders: Nothing — this app is invisible. The `@wordpress/commands` portal renders the palette UI elsewhere in the DOM.

interactions.trigger: User opens palette (Mod+K or other binding)
interactions.effect: `@wordpress/commands` invokes the registered loader, gets the derived commands, and surfaces them. Selecting an entry calls its `callback({ close })` which calls `trigger(invoke)` then falls back to the runtime router's `navigate(path)` when invoke didn't handle (or wasn't present), then closes the palette.

a11y.focus-management: `@wordpress/commands` owns palette focus when open (focus trap inside the modal, return focus on close). This app only contributes commands; it does not render UI.

constraints.note: Returns `null`. All visual surface area lives in the `@wordpress/commands` portal. Tests that look for shell-rendered DOM should expect nothing.

Screens with `{param}` placeholders or `/*` wildcard suffixes are skipped — `Go to /posts/{id}` isn't a valid invocation because the user can't pick the captured value from a command list. Parameterized navigation needs a different surface (search-based, entity-based) that's out of scope here.
Commands without a `label` are keyboard-only and handled by `BindingsConsumer`'s keystroke path. They never appear in the palette so users discover them only via the shortcut documentation.

Palette names use `encodeURIComponent(id)` so ids with slashes or other URL-unsafe characters produce distinct names without colliding under `@wordpress/commands`'s duplicate-name rejection. The unified `core/admin-shell/palette-<id>` prefix means screen ids and command ids share the namespace — first-write wins on collision.

Manifest declares `core:modal: true` + `core:dismiss-on: [Escape, backdrop-click]` + `core:triggerable: true`. The kernel's region renderer applies focus trap + ARIA modal + backdrop dismiss. The triggerable flag lets admin.json's `commands[].invoke` map keystrokes to this app.

The `$schema` reference still points at `admin-app-v2.json` because this manifest hasn't been migrated to the v3 app-manifest shape yet. The doc sweep in roadmap §3d.4 flips this. Behavior consumed by the runtime is already v3 (`commands[]` + `screens[]`).

design-system-leakage.purpose: Command registration. The package owns the palette UI.
Per-command icons resolved through the kernel icon registry — bundled `core:default` engine ships the `@wordpress/icons` table.
URL navigation — same entry point `BindingsConsumer` uses, so the palette callback path mirrors the keystroke path exactly.
App-trigger dispatch for commands declaring `invoke`. Returns whether a registered handler claimed the trigger, gating the `navigate` fallback for compound entries.
